parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The expression to evaluate cumulatively from the start of the year to the current date.

parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: A date column from a marked date table.
parameters.examNote: Must come from a date table marked as a date table. Requires a continuous, gap-free date table.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: An additional filter to apply during evaluation.
parameters.examNote: Rarely used — the function already handles YTD date logic automatically.

parameters.name: year_end_date
parameters.description: The last day of the fiscal year if different from December 31st.
parameters.examNote: Use "6/30" for a fiscal year ending June 30th. Format is MM/DD.

summary: TOTALYTD computes a year-to-date cumulative total from January 1st (or the fiscal year start) through the current date in context. Equivalent to CALCULATE(expression, DATESYTD(dates)) but more concise.

examples.label: Cumulative year-to-date sales
examples.explanation: By March, the YTD total is 100 + 150 + 200 = 450. TOTALYTD accumulates from the start of the year to the current month's end date.

steps: Current filter context contains a date (e.g., March 2024)
TOTALYTD replaces the date filter with all dates from Jan 1 2024 through Mar 31 2024
The expression is evaluated across this expanded date range
Result is the cumulative total from the start of the year

commonTraps: Requires a continuous date table with no gaps — missing dates cause incorrect YTD cutoffs.
TOTALYTD resets at the start of each calendar year unless year_end_date is specified for fiscal year calculations.
TOTALYTD is equivalent to CALCULATE(expression, DATESYTD(dates)) — both approaches appear on the exam.
